newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait welcomes oil deal for Iraqi people's sake.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait welcomes oil deal for Iraqi people's sake.

text.p: Kuwait on Tuesday welcomed Iraq's acceptance of U.N. terms for limited oil exports.
Asked if Kuwait welcomed the move by former occupier Iraq, Crown Prince and Prime Minister Sheikh Saad al-Abdulla al-Sabah told reporters: "For the Iraqi people without hesitation."
The Iraqi people are "suffering from lack of medicine, lack of food and lack of everything they need," Sheikh Saad said.
The United Nations imposed stringent sanctions on Iraq after it seized Kuwait in 1990. A U.S.-led multinational force liberated Kuwait in 1991.

Iraq on Monday accepted U.N. terms to implement a deal signed in May allowing it to sell oil worth $2 billion over six months to pay for food and medicine and some U.N. operation related to the crisis over Kuwait's seven-month occupation.
